summary: Full target-level pass over N.1–N.8, continuing seven existing part packets without redeclaring their 130 IDs. Adds number-ring hermitian finite generation and all-integer-degree Bott-inverted arithmetic tables. The inheritance manifest records every earlier target, its current contract, and its owner; the reader includes the later rank, ramification, e-invariant, wild-kernel and explicit-certificate refinements. Corrects the K3/Bloch direction and narrows duplicate supplier interfaces. Complete means that every target is planned; the exact supplier and source-proof gaps below prevent closure. All implementation remains unchecked.

nodes.title: Finite generation of number-ring L-groups
nodes.statement: For a number field F, finite set S of finite primes and O=O_(F,S), both periodic groups L^s_n(O;ε) and L^q_n(O;ε) are finitely generated abelian groups for every integer n and ε∈{+1,−1}. Here s is periodic symmetric L-theory and q is periodic quadratic L-theory, not a genuine connective flavour.
hypotheses: S is finite; the ring involution is the identity and the coefficient line is O with sign ε.
The fraction field has characteristic zero; the assertion includes dyadic primes without assuming 2 invertible.
proofSteps: Use GN.6’s arithmetic Witt signature theorem: W^s(O) is an extension of a finite group by a free group of rank r1. Pic(O) is a quotient of the finite class group of O_F. This exact arithmetic signature contract is requested below, not inferred from a field Witt computation.
Import DA.0/integral-injectivity to embed W^q(O) in W^s(O). Thus the quadratic Witt group is finitely generated by the noetherian property of Z.

Use DA.1/global-symmetric and DA.3/number-field-quadratic: all other entries are finite residue Witt groups, Pic(O)/2 and the finite dyadic correction A(O). Subgroups and extensions of finitely generated abelian groups are finitely generated.
Apply the imported sign shift and four-periodicity. This is the arithmetic finiteness corollary; it does not construct L-theory or reprove the Dedekind tables.

sources.match: Reduces all periodic L-group degrees to symmetric and quadratic Witt groups and Picard groups of a number ring.

acceptance: For O=Z the symmetric residues mod 4 are Z,Z/2,0,0 and the quadratic residues Z,0,Z/2,0.
Do not infer finite generation for an arbitrary Dedekind domain or infinite S from this statement.

nodes.title: Finite generation in every genuine flavour
nodes.statement: For O=O_(F,S), F a number field and S finite, every integer m,n and ε=±1, L_n(O;Q_ε^(≥m)) is finitely generated. The coefficient and Poincaré structures are GN.6’s; the superscript is the genuine quadratic-to-symmetric filtration.
hypotheses: m and n range over Z, and ε is the standard sign coefficient.
proofSteps: The structure Q^(≥m) is m-quadratic and (2−m)-symmetric. Import the quadratic comparison range from HK.5 and the symmetric comparison range from HK.7.
For n≤2m−2 the map L^q_n→L_n(Q^(≥m)) is surjective; for n≥2m−1 the map L_n(Q^(≥m))→L^s_n is injective. These adjacent integer ranges exhaust all n.
Apply number-ring-l-finite-generation and closure of finitely generated Z-modules under quotients and subgroups. No periodicity of the genuine flavour is assumed.

sources.locator: Corollary 2.3.18, p. 48; Corollaries 1.2.12 and 1.3.9, pp. 18 and 31
sources.match: The two comparison ranges give finite generation of each genuine L-group, including the boundary degrees.

acceptance: Check n=2m−2 through surjectivity and n=2m−1 through injectivity.
No equality of classical quadratic and symmetric forms at 2 is used.

nodes.title: Hermitian finite generation over number rings
nodes.statement: Let O=O_(F,S) for a number field F and a finite set S of finite primes. For ε=±1 and every n≥0, the classical ε-symmetric and ε-quadratic Grothendieck–Witt groups GW^s_(cl,n)(O;ε) and GW^q_(cl,n)(O;ε) are finitely generated abelian groups. No choice of quadratic refinement, inversion of 2, or vanishing of real places is assumed.
hypotheses: Classical groups are nonnegative-degree groups. The genuine derived flavours used in the proof retain their integer indexing.
proofSteps: Quillen finite generation supplies each π_b K(O) for b≥0. The connective homotopy-orbit spectral sequence H_a(C2;K_b(O))⇒π_(a+b)(K(O)_(hC2)) has only finitely many terms on each diagonal. Each is finitely generated: finite-group homology of a finitely generated abelian coefficient group has this property. The exact finite-type spectral-sequence contract is requested from H.6.

Use the fundamental fibre sequence K(O)_(hC2)→GW(O;Q^(≥m))→L(O;Q^(≥m)) and the preceding genuine-L theorem. The long exact sequence expresses each GW group as an extension of a quotient and a subgroup of finitely generated groups.

Import GN.6’s Hebestreit–Steimle classical comparison and HK.8’s symmetric/quadratic fibre sequences to obtain both classical flavours in every n≥0. This is Corollary 2.3.19, restated as introduction Corollary 8. The low quadratic degrees are covered by the supplied classical fibre sequence, not by extending a comparison valid only in degrees ≥4.

sources.locator: Corollary 8, p. 5; Corollaries 2.3.18–2.3.19 and proofs, p. 48
sources.match: Combines arithmetic K finiteness, homotopy orbits, genuine L comparison and the classical comparison to prove both classical GW finiteness assertions.

acceptance: Apply to Z and Z[1/2], for both signs, including n=0,1,2,3.
Keep finite generation separate from the explicit hermitian group tables of GN Part II.
An infinite set S supplies no finite-generation conclusion by this proof.

nodes.title: Degree and twist convention for Adams pieces
nodes.statement: For j∈Z and ε∈{+1,−1}, define the slot of the ε-piece of degree 2j to be (s,t)=(0,j) if ε=(−1)^j and (s,t)=(2,j+1) otherwise. Its interpretation is H^s_et(X,Z/q(t)). The slot stores indices only; it does not define a new K-group, twist, cohomology carrier or Adams eigenspace.
hypotheses: q=p^r with p odd prime and r≥1 when the slot is interpreted in the arithmetic tables.
Positive and negative refer to dualization ψ^(−1), not complex conjugation on the cyclotomic field.
proofSteps: In M.7 descent E2^(s,2t)=H^s(X,Z/q(t)), the total degree is 2t−s. The only possible even-degree terms for a dimension-two arithmetic scheme have s=0 or 2.
Adams weights make the signs (−1)^j and (−1)^(j+1) opposite. The two explicit cases therefore determine the slot.

sources.locator: Lemmas 2.11 and 2.14, pp. 244 and 246; descent (2.6), pp. 241–242
sources.match: The even-degree tables specify the cohomological degree and twist of each dualization eigenspace.

acceptance: At degree zero the positive slot is H0(0), the negative slot H2(1).
At degree −2 the positive slot is H2(0), the negative slot H0(−1).

uses.where: N.6, the two all-degree Bott tables
uses.how: selects the exact twist and cohomological degree without a natural-number truncation.
fixes all integer k, including k=0 and negative k, for the requested eigenspace contracts.

nodes.title: Canonical arithmetic Adams edge splitting
nodes.statement: Let q=p^r with p odd and r≥1, X=Spec Z[1/p] or Spec Z[ζ_q,1/p]. For every j∈Z, the Bott/étale descent filtration gives 0→H²_et(X,Z/q(j+1))→K^β_(2j)(X;Z/q)→H⁰_et(X,Z/q(j))→0. The kernel has dualization sign (−1)^(j+1), the quotient sign (−1)^j. Since 2 is a unit modulo q, restriction to these eigenspaces canonically splits this exact sequence. In odd degree, the sole term gives K^β_(2j−1)(X;Z/q)≃H¹_et(X,Z/q(j)), with sign (−1)^j. The equivalences are the descent edge maps on the indicated eigenspaces.
hypotheses: K^β is M.7’s Bott-inverted finite coefficient spectrum, indexed over all integers.
The schemes have odd-p étale cohomological dimension ≤2; this exact global-arithmetic contract is requested below.
No associative ring structure on a mod-3 Moore spectrum is assumed; Bott inversion and operations are supplied at spectrum level by M.7.
proofSteps: Import the convergent descent sequence and cd≤2. Odd internal rows vanish. All d_r are zero: for r even their target internal row is odd, and for r odd≥3 they leave the cohomological strip. The filtration has a single odd term and two even terms.
Use M.7 Adams weights. On total degree 2j, the H² and H⁰ terms have opposite eigenvalues. For the involution T=ψ^(−1), the endomorphisms (1±T)/2 are complementary idempotents over Z/q.

The eigenpart of the quotient sign maps isomorphically to H⁰; the other eigenpart is exactly H². Inverting that restricted edge map gives the unique sign-compatible splitting. Maps of the descent filtration commuting with T preserve it.

sources.match: Cohomological dimension collapses descent; the opposite dualization weights split the two even terms canonically at odd modulus.

acceptance: At j=0 the rank class has sign + and the reduced Picard class sign −.
No splitting by (1±T)/2 is asserted for even q.
The odd-degree group has one sign only.

uses.where: N.6, cyclotomic and rational Bott tables
uses.how: gives the canonical maps and resolves the even-degree extension.
supplies eigenspaces without assuming a noncanonical abstract group splitting.

api.name: bottEvenExact
api.statement: The named H² inclusion and H⁰ quotient are the convergent descent edge maps in the displayed sequence.

api.name: bottAdamsPiece
api.statement: Use Module.End.eigenspace ψ^(−1) ε over Z/q, rather than defining another eigenspace.

api.name: bottEvenEdgeEquiv
api.statement: Restrict the edge maps to their signs to identify the two pieces with H²(j+1) and H⁰(j).

api.name: bottOddEdgeEquiv

api.name: bottEdge_natural
api.statement: Any morphism of these descent filtrations commuting with ψ^(−1) commutes with the restricted edges, their inverses and the splitting; identity and composition laws follow.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic Bott-inverted cohomology table
nodes.statement: For q=p^r, p an odd prime, r≥1, put X=Spec Z[ζ_q,1/p]. For every k∈Z, the canonical ψ^(−1) eigenspaces are K^β_(4k−2)(X;Z/q)^+≃H²_et(X,Z/q(2k)), K^β_(4k−2)^−≃H⁰_et(X,Z/q(2k−1)), K^β_(4k)^+≃H⁰_et(X,Z/q(2k)), and K^β_(4k)^−≃H²_et(X,Z/q(2k+1)). Also K^β_(2k−1)≃H¹_et(X,Z/q(k)), on which ψ^(−1) acts by (−1)^k. Negative twists and negative K^β degrees retain their integer meaning.
hypotheses: The notation μ_q^⊗t means the étale Tate twist Z/q(t), including the dual twist for t<0.
The signs are dualization eigenspaces over Z/q, with 2 invertible.
proofSteps: Specialize bott-adams-edge-splitting to X.
In degree 4k−2 set j=2k−1; in degree 4k set j=2k. Substitute the two parity signs; retain the actual restricted edge equivalences.
Use the odd single-term edge with j=k. No bounded-below truncation is applied after Bott inversion.

sources.match: Provides the four even Adams pieces and the single odd cohomology group for every integer weight.

acceptance: k=0 gives degree −2: + is H²(0) and − is H⁰(−1); degree 0: + is H⁰(0) and − is H²(1).
k=1 gives degree 2: + is H²(2), − is H⁰(1).
Odd degrees one and three have respectively negative and positive dualization.

Also K^β_(2k−1)≃H¹_et(X,Z/q(k)), on which ψ^(−1) acts by (−1)^k. Negative twists and negative K^β degrees retain their integer meaning.

The signs are dualization eigenspaces over Z/q, with 2 invertible.

In degree 4k−2 set j=2k−1; in degree 4k set j=2k. Substitute the two parity signs; retain the actual restricted edge equivalences.

nodes.title: Ordinary-to-Bott comparison with its degree-one exception
nodes.statement: For q=p^r with p odd and r≥1, and R equal to Z or Z[ζ_q], let R′=R[1/p]. The canonical map K_i(R′;Z/q)→K^β_i(R′;Z/q) is an isomorphism for every i≥0. The map K_i(R;Z/q)→K^β_i(R;Z/q) is an isomorphism for i=0 or i≥2. In degree one localization gives K_1(R′;Z/q)≃K_1(R;Z/q)⊕Z/q; this abstract direct sum is not declared a natural splitting without a chosen prime generator. Bott-inverted localization K^β_*(R)→K^β_*(R′) is an isomorphism in all integer degrees.
hypotheses: R is one of these two rings; the unique prime above p in the cyclotomic ring is principal and has residue F_p.
No ordinary negative-degree comparison, and no ordinary degree-one comparison before inversion, is asserted.
proofSteps: Use M.7/s-integer-comparison-range for i≥1 over R′, with finite coefficients; the degree-zero comparison is injective.

The degree-zero filtration has H⁰(X,Z/q)=Z/q and H²(X,μ_q)=Pic(R′)/q: the Brauer q-part vanishes because there is one finite place in S and odd coefficients have no real-place contribution. The Kummer exact sequence and global Brauer reciprocity provide this exact calculation, requested from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3. Both K0(R′)/q and the target have order q·#(Pic(R′)/q), so the injection is onto.

Localization at the single p-prime has coefficient residue K(F_p;Z/q) concentrated in degree zero. Its map to K0(R;Z/q) vanishes because the prime is principal. The long exact sequence changes ordinary coefficients only in degree one. The abstract extra cyclic summand follows from the unit valuation at the chosen principal generator.

The residue spectrum becomes zero after Bott inversion, hence the inverted localization is an equivalence in all degrees. Combine with the two tables; no associative product at q=3 is introduced in this proof.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.9 and Lemma 2.10, pp. 242–243; final assertions of Lemmas 2.11 and 2.14, pp. 244–247
sources.match: The zero-degree order argument upgrades injectivity; the principal p-prime accounts for the sole ordinary localization exception.

acceptance: For R=Z, the new degree-one class is the valuation of p, with order q modulo q-th powers.
For R=Z[ζ_q], use 1−ζ_q as a generator of the unique p-prime.
k≤0 entries of the Bott tables do not become statements about ordinary negative algebraic K-groups.

nodes.title: The arithmetic K3 examples
nodes.statement: The odd structure theorem gives K3(Z)≃K3(Q)≃Z/48 and K3(Z[i])≃K3(Q(i))≃Z⊕Z/24. The ring-to-field isomorphisms are the natural localization maps; the displayed free-plus-torsion decompositions are abstract group isomorphisms and no canonical generator or splitting is claimed. The computations of K0(Z), K1(Z), K2(Z) and K2(Q) are imported from Z.6, U.6 and T.5, and K2(Z[i])=0 remains the independent Tate certificate.
hypotheses: Use n=3, j=2 in N.5, with w2(Q)=w2(Q(i))=24 from N.4.
The signatures are (1,0) for Q and (0,1) for Q(i).
proofSteps: Import the real mod-eight N.5 theorem at n≡3, r1=1,r2=0: its torsion order is 2w2(Q)=48 and the residual (Z/2)^(r1−1) is trivial.
Import the totally imaginary N.5 theorem at j=2, r2=1 and w2(Q(i))=24. The ring-to-field maps are isomorphisms by N.2/Soulé.

Export these groups to K3BlochGroups V.5. That roadmap uses its Milnor/decomposable and indecomposable quotient machinery to classify the classes; it supplies none of the arithmetic group calculation here.

sources.locator: Theorem VI.9.5, book p. 519 (PDF p. 527); Example VI.2.1.2, book p. 470 (PDF p. 478)
sources.match: The general odd-group formula and the cyclotomic w2 calculation give both arithmetic K3 examples without a Bloch-group input.

acceptance: The real factor is 48 rather than w2(Q)=24.
The Gaussian example has a rank-one free part; the vanishing of its K2 tame kernel gives no argument for this free rank.
No prerequsite path through K3BlochGroups V.5 is introduced.

contractRevision.statement: For a number field F and S a set of finite primes, the determinant identifies K1(O_(F,S)) with O_(F,S)^×, compatibly with inclusion into F^× and with N.1’s transfer norm. Import the Bass–Milnor–Serre determinant theorem from KTheoryLowDegrees U.4/U.6; N.1 supplies the arithmetic S-integer specialization and comparisons. Finite generation of units requires finite S.
contractRevision.reason: The low-degree calculation is owned by KTheoryLowDegrees; use the pinned Set.integer and Set.unit carriers.
proofSteps: Import the determinant and SK1=0 from U.4/U.6, then identify its codomain with the existing S-unit carrier. Finite generation is Tau Ceti’s unit_fg_of_units when S is finite. Use N.1’s explicit extension and relative norm comparisons for the two functorial maps.

contractRevision.statement: For O_(F,S)⊂F use SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.3/dedekind-localisation-sequence with residues at the finite primes outside S. Its boundary in degree one is the divisor map, and the class map sends e_p to [p]^(−1). N.2 adds arithmetic finite support, field-extension compatibilities and degree-specific injectivity; it does not reconstruct the general sequence.
contractRevision.reason: RT-AREA-ktheory-2/42 assigns the general sequence to S.3.
proofSteps: Apply S.3’s exact sequence to the existing Dedekind S-integer ring. Identify its closed points with the primes outside S using the pinned spectrum equivalence. Import the divisor and tame-symbol boundary normalizations; prove arithmetic finite support in the separate N.2 target.

contractRevision.statement: The degree-zero and degree-one end is S.3’s divisor/Picard sequence. In degree two import T.5/s-integer-tame-kernel-sequence: 0→K2(O_(F,S))→K2(F)→⊕_(p∉S)k(p)^×→0. Comparing O_F to O_(F,S) instead gives the finite sum over p∈S. N.2 supplies arithmetic compatibility of these already-owned rows, not another tame-kernel theorem.
contractRevision.reason: RT-AREA-ktheory-1/9 and 2/42; distinguish the two complementary prime sets.
proofSteps: Import the divisor/Picard end from S.3 and both complementary degree-two S-integer sequences from T.5. Use the finite-field K2 vanishing and Bass–Milnor–Serre only in the T.5 supplier proof; N.2 proves the arithmetic identifications commute with these maps.

contractRevision.statement: For a finite extension E/F of number fields and T the finite primes of E above S, transfer commutes with the localization sequences through residue norms. Restriction uses the ramification-weighted residue pullback: its p→q component is e(q/p) times the residue-field scalar extension. N.2/ramified-residue-pullback through N.2/s-integer-restriction-compatibility supplies the full restriction contract; an unweighted pullback is asserted only in the unramified case.
contractRevision.reason: The five N.2 follow-up targets close the old ramification gap.
proofSteps: For transfer, use restriction of scalars and residue-field transfer under dévissage. For pullback, use the five ramified follow-up targets: the pullback of a residue module has length e(q/p), so the q-coordinate is e(q/p) times residue scalar extension. The tensor filtrations and their additive K-theory maps give the commuting square.

contractRevision.statement: For an m-dimensional F-vector space V, the proper-layer poset of N.3 has nerve homotopy equivalent to the unreduced suspension of the Tits building imported from R.1. Thus its only reduced integral homology is the imported Steinberg module in degree m−1; rank one uses the empty-building convention and reduced degree-zero homology. The arithmetic comparison of the layer poset with the imported building is the N.3 target; the building and Solomon–Tits theorem are R.1 targets.
contractRevision.reason: Retains the rank-filtration-specific comparison while removing duplicated foundations.
proofSteps: Identify the comma-category layer poset with N.3’s proper-layer poset. Apply the rank-filtration-specific suspension comparison of Kahn Proposition 4.3.1–4.3.2. Use the imported R.1 building and Solomon–Tits homology, retaining the rank-one empty-building convention.

contractRevision.statement: For a projective O_F-lattice P of rank m≥1, H_i(Aut_(O_F)(P);St(P⊗F)) is finitely generated for every i≥0. This is the arithmetic specialization of BorelRegulators:R.1/steinberg-duality-finiteness, which includes nonfree P, the orientation character and finite-index descent. N.3 uses it in Quillen’s rank filtration and proves none of the building or duality foundation again.
contractRevision.reason: RT-AREA-ktheory-1/1: R.1 is the sole Tits-building, Steinberg and Borel–Serre owner.
proofSteps: Specialize R.1/steinberg-duality-finiteness to the order O_F in F and the actual projective lattice P. That theorem supplies the orientation twist and finite-index descent, including the nonfree case. Use its finitely generated homology groups as the coefficients in Quillen’s rank spectral sequence.

contractRevision.statement: For F a number field, S finite and n≥2, the natural map K_n(O_F)⊗Q→K_n(O_(F,S))⊗Q is an isomorphism. Consequently the rank is r1+r2 for n≡1 mod4, r2 for n≡3 mod4 and 0 for n even, using R.3’s rank formula for O_F. The S-integer extension is owned here: finite-S localization and finite-field positive K-groups give its proof. Degree one instead has rank r1+r2+|S|−1.
contractRevision.reason: RT-AREA-ktheory-1/7: R.3 treats orders, N.3:ranks treats localization.
proofSteps: Apply the finite-S localization defect theorem to the actual map K_n(O_F)→K_n(O_(F,S)). For n≥2 the residue terms in positive degrees are finite by L.1, so rationalization makes this map an isomorphism. Import R.3’s orders-only rank formula. Degree one uses the S-unit sequence and never this formula.

contractRevision.statement: Let F be a number field with r_1 > 0 real embeddings and r_2 complex places, and O_S a ring of S-integers in F. For each odd n ≥ 3, with i = (n + 1)/2, K_n(O_S) ≅ K_n(F) and K_n(F) ≅ ℤ^{r_1+r_2} ⊕ ℤ/w_i(F) for n ≡ 1 (mod 8); ℤ^{r_2} ⊕ ℤ/2w_i(F) ⊕ (ℤ/2)^{r_1−1} for n ≡ 3 (mod 8); ℤ^{r_1+r_2} ⊕ ℤ/(w_i(F)/2) for n ≡ 5 (mod 8); ℤ^{r_2} ⊕ ℤ/w_i(F) for n ≡ 7 (mod 8). In the class n ≡ 5 (mod 8) the index i is odd, so w_i^{(2)}(F) = 2 and w_i(F)/2 is an odd integer: K_n(F) has no two-primary torsion. These groups are determined by r_1, r_2 and w_i(F). The direct-sum decompositions are of abstract groups and are not natural; what is natural is the identification of the ℓ-primary torsion through the comparison maps (N.5/odd-torsion-at-a-prime-where-cd-is-two for ℓ odd, and for ℓ = 2 the ℚ_2/ℤ_2-coefficient computation of MotivicEtaleKTheory M.7, Theorem VI.9.4, induced by the morphism to the real places), including the non-split extension that produces ℤ/2w_i(F) ⊕ (ℤ/2)^{r_1−1}.
contractRevision.reason: The group table is retained. The real differential and extension input is now M.7/real-place-correction and /dyadic-s-integer-extensions, preceded by M.7/suslin-real-comparison and the real KO/BO request; full M.8 is not a prerequisite of this arithmetic table.
proofSteps: Use M.7’s named Suslin-real and real-place spectral-sequence comparisons to determine the dyadic differentials and extensions; its nontrivial extension produces 2w_j in residue three. Combine with the odd-primary calculation and finite generation/ranks. In residue five retain the factor w_j/2 and prove its divisibility; abstract splittings are not natural e-invariant maps. The N.5 follow-up supplies the extension normal form and edge comparison, with G-Coefficient and G-ChernBoundary explicitly open.

contractRevision.statement: Import the tame subgroup and its identification with K2(O_F) from T.5/unramified-subgroup and /tame-kernel-sequence. For i≥1 define the raw completion kernel WK^raw_(2i)(F)=ker(K_(2i)(F)→∏_v K_(2i)(F_v)), using every finite and real place. This is separate from N.6/symbol-wild-kernel and /cohomological-wild-kernel; their comparison is only the explicitly proved degree-two theorem, or a higher statement conditional on gap G-WildHigher. Infinite products here do not replace the finite-support direct sums of localization.
contractRevision.reason: RT-AREA-ktheory-1/9 and the N.6 follow-up distinguish imported tame symbols from higher local finite quotients.
proofSteps: Use T.5’s subgroup and localization identification for the tame kernel. Define the raw kernel as the intersection of the actual completion-map kernels, including real places. The completion/localization square and Soulé’s injectivity place it inside the finite integral group. The separate N.6/raw-and-symbol-kernel-boundary theorem imports this definition and supplies the degree-two comparison using Moore; the higher comparison is conditional on G-WildHigher. The comparison theorem is not a prerequisite for defining the raw kernel.

contractRevision.statement: Let div K_(2i)(F)=∩_(m≥1)mK_(2i)(F), the subgroup of elements divisible by every positive integer. For the symbol wild kernel K^w_(2i)(F), the N.6 follow-up records div⊆K^w with index at most 2, equality for even i or a nonspecial field, and the special odd dyadic obstruction. The exceptional odd dyadic proof remains conditional on G-WildExceptional. For i=1 the symbol and raw completion kernels agree by Moore’s uniquely divisible local kernel. For i≥2 no raw-kernel equality follows without G-WildHigher. No largest-divisible-subgroup interpretation of div is used.
contractRevision.reason: The old K-book equality is not accepted as a general raw higher-kernel theorem.
proofSteps: Use the N.6 follow-up’s finite-coefficient image, cohomological comparison and special dyadic obstruction targets for the symbol-kernel theorem. Its exceptional odd dyadic branch remains conditional on G-WildExceptional. For the raw kernel use only degree two, where the local Moore kernel is uniquely divisible. The higher Q_p/Z_p obstruction is G-WildHigher.

contractRevision.statement: In the restriction morphism, identify K_0(k(p)) and K_0(k(q)) with ℤ by rank, and K_1 of each residue field with its unit group by determinant. Then ρ_0 has q-coordinate e(q/p)x_p and ρ_1 has q-coordinate res(u_p)^{e(q/p)}. Consequently normalized additive orders satisfy v_q(res x)=e(q/p)v_p(x), and the imported degree-two boundary β satisfies β_q(res z)=res(β_p z)^{e(q/p)}. Adopt the K-book right-linear boundary convention β_p{a,b}=(-1)^{v_p(a)v_p(b)} overline(b^{v_p(a)}/a^{v_p(b)}), so β_p{π,u}=ū; it is the inverse of T.3’s left-oriented tameSymbol(a,b). In either convention the e-th-power compatibility is identical. On the K_0 integral terms this commutes with extension of divisor ideals pB=∏_{q|p}q^e and the class-map sign [A/p]=[A]−[p]. Import the arithmetic degree-two exact sequence, including injectivity, from T.5; do not derive it here.
contractRevision.reason: The refinement proves restriction before N.2/localisation-sequence-and-finite-extensions compiles restriction and transfer. Its transfer comparison uses the independent S.3 finite-pushforward theorem, avoiding a circular prerequisite through that compilation.
proofSteps: Use field rank and determinant comparisons already supplied by N.1’s classical K_0/K_1 imports and N.2/the-three-classical-rows. Scalar extension preserves vector-space dimension and maps a unit to its residue-field image; multiplying a K_1 class e times is taking the e-th power.

Apply finite-extension-restriction-compatibility to the imported S.3 unit-valuation boundary and the T.3 comparison (through the existing S.3/N.2 boundary contracts). This gives the additive valuation and tame-boundary equations without constructing any boundary again.

Check the valuation equality against pinned HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_liesOver, converting its multiplicative power equation to normalized additive order and converting the primed two-ideal index using Ideal.ramificationIdx'_eq_ramificationIdx.

On symbols write a=π^r u, b=π^s v. The target orders are er and es. Reducing b^{er}/a^{es} gives the e-th power of the source quotient; the sign agrees because e²rs−ers is even. The extra unit in the image of π cancels. This directly checks the convention and is a test of the imported naturality result.
For the class map use [A/p]=[A]−[p] from the imported S.3 row. Its pullback becomes [B]−[pB]=Σ_{q|p}e(q/p)([B]−[q]) via the coefficient filtration, so the inverse-Picard convention is respected.

Use the existing T.5 tame-kernel, S-integer and relative S-integer exact-sequence nodes as imports; all three exact statements were read in the T.3 packet. That packet remains partial with a needs-changes review, so these are mathematical contracts rather than reviewed implementation claims. S.3/boundary-finite-pushforward-naturality supplies the transfer morphism, which goes B → A and uses residue transfers/norms without an e coefficient; this node goes A → B.

contractRevision.statement: For F=Q(i), the Tate norm-filtration certificate proves K2(Z[i])=0. Independently N.8/arithmetic-k3-examples gives K3(Z[i])≃K3(Q(i))≃Z⊕Z/24 from the N.5 odd structure theorem and w2(Q(i))=24. These statements use no Bloch-group calculation. requests.need: Export, or route to the existing global-forms owner, the number-ring signature theorem: for O=O_(F,S), F a number field and S finite, W^s(O) has finite signature kernel and signature image a rank-r1 sublattice of Z^r1. Include finite Pic(O) under localization and the characteristic-zero injection W^q(O)→W^s(O). Supply the fundamental genuine GW fibre sequence and the nonnegative classical symmetric/quadratic comparisons used in Corollary 2.3.19. Import DA.0/integral-injectivity where it already supplies the injection.

For a connective spectrum E with C2 action and every π_b(E) finitely generated, give the strongly convergent homotopy-orbit spectral sequence H_a(C2;π_bE)⇒π_(a+b)(E_hC2); each diagonal is finite and its abutment is finitely generated. Also retain the exact Q_l/Z_l coefficient-colimit, Bockstein and localization compatibilities needed by N.5. Existing H.6/qp-zp-coefficients supplies the object; the finite-type and edge compatibility statements are the requested additions.

For a connected CW H-space X, including nonzero π1, prove simplicity (π1 abelian acting trivially on higher homotopy) and that integral homology finitely generated in each degree implies every π_j(X) finitely generated. Give the Postnikov/Serre-class proof. This extends the plus/simple-space direction; a simply connected version alone does not suffice for BQ.

Supply the actual finite-coefficient localization fibre sequence and boundary projection formula for the K.7 product action, with natural reduction/Bockstein maps. At unsafe moduli 2,3,4,8 state only the coherent spectrum/module operations that exist. For Soulé lift to a safe prime power M, use its product, then reduce to m; never infer a ring structure on K(R;Z/m) from this reduction. Include the finite-perfect localization comparison used to invert the principal p-prime in ordinary-to-bott-comparison-range.

Use the existing named Suslin-real-comparison, real-place-correction and dyadic-s-integer-extensions before N.5. Export equivariance of the separably closed torsion identification, its coefficient colimit, and compatibility of the descent edge with connecting maps. The early edge-normalised torsion map must depend on M.7 and not on the full M.8 Chern/regulator family. For Bott tables retain the spectrum-level ψ^(−1) operation for every odd prime power, including q=3.

In the early topological layer, supply real KO/BO, real Bott 8-periodicity, the coefficient comparisons and π_n(BO;Z/m) used by the existing M.7/suslin-real-comparison node. Complex KU/ku and Clifford-algebra periodicity alone do not compute these groups.

Export cd_p≤2 for X=Spec O_(F,S)[1/p] at odd p, the Kummer exact sequence and the Brauer local-global exact sequence with arithmetic-Frobenius normalization. For X=Spec Z[1/p] or Z[ζ_(p^r),1/p], with exactly one finite prime inverted, deduce Br(X)[p^r]=0 and H²(X,μ_(p^r))≃Pic(X)/p^r. Keep real places and the sum-of-invariants condition: simply omitting the local term at p would be incorrect.

Provide the finite-field/wreath-product map and a detected Harris–Segal torsion summand, with its original proof (Harris–Segal Theorem 3.1) or a verified independent argument. The abstract odd group formula does not choose a natural summand. Reuse L.1/k-theory-mod-m, /bott-element and /mod-m-products for their actual, currently restricted statements. The regular-prime finite-coefficient module and its exact generator degrees need their own proof, not just these object definitions.

Export proved Kummer criterion/congruences and the finite cyclotomic Herbrand–Ribet character statement needed in N.7, with arithmetic Bernoulli indices: for even a, 2≤a≤p−3, p|num B_a iff the mod-p class-group eigenspace ω^(1−a) is nonzero. The denominator 1/(p−1) of the character projector is a unit modulo p; integral projectors without this inversion are not supplied. Washington is not a source obtained in this run; use a freely available original or a maintainer-cleared copy.

inheritancePolicy: The checker forbids declaring a node ID in two packets of the same roadmap.
